lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Caring for Home and Shared Spaces
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: everything needs a home

objective: Learners assign a specific "home" location to five loose household items and practice returning items to those homes with fading adult support across two rounds.
scenario: The learner gathers five loose items that don't currently have an obvious storage spot (for example a phone charger, scissors, a specific toy, a hairbrush, a stack of mail) and, with an adult the first time and alone the second, decides on and uses a consistent home for each item.
safetyNotes: Use respectful, non-shaming language if an item's home fails on the first try.

simulationAlternative.description: If the household doesn't have five clearly homeless items on hand, the learner instead selects five items from a printed or hand-drawn room scene, proposes a home for each based on how it's used, and explains their reasoning the same way as the guided task.

materials: five loose household items without a fixed spot

tasks.directions: Before assigning homes, notice: do these five items already have a place they usually end up, or do they end up in different places every time?

prompts.text: Describe the current, inconsistent pattern for each of the five items.

tasks.directions: With your adult, choose one home for each of the five items and put each item there for the first time.

prompts.text: Each of the five items now has one specific spot, not 'somewhere in this room.'
I said out loud why that spot makes sense for that item (near where it is used, easy to reach, etc.).
My adult only helped me decide, not put the items away for me.

tasks.directions: The next day, without your adult's help, find all five items (wherever they ended up) and return each one to its assigned home.

prompts.text: Were all five items still where you left them, or did one drift? What happened to it?

tasks.directions: Reflect on the hardest item to keep in its home.

prompts.text: What made that item's home less 'sticky' than the others, and what would you change about the spot you chose?

remediation: If an item's home keeps failing (drifting back to a random spot), reteach by testing whether the assigned home is actually on the item's normal path of use — move the home to a spot the learner passes when they finish using the item, then retest for two more days.
extension: Assign homes for five additional items in a different room and compare, in writing, whether homes were easier or harder to choose the second time.
